title: Auditable Policy Compiler and SIEM Export Contract
content:
Purpose and scope:

This document proposes an "auditable policy compiler" that converts RBAC-v2 high-level authorization rules and grants into two artifacts: (1) a deterministic runtime policy blob used at enforcement points (API gateways, serving runtime, console routes), and (2) a signed audit bundle that can be exported to SIEMs and evidence automation pipelines. The goal is to make permission decisions both verifiable after the fact and lightweight at runtime, while enabling automated compliance checks and forensics across Dedicated/Private/Hosted deployments.

Context and motivation:

Current pain points observed during RBAC-v2 prototyping:
- Divergence between policy expressed in the authorization UI/Confluence and runtime checks (drift).
- Audit logs are noisy and inconsistent across services; mapping to entitlement changes is manual.
- SIEM ingestion expects a stable schema but enforcement representations change with iterative policy updates.
- For canary and staged rollouts we need a minimal payload to compare decisions and collect counterfactual evidence without impacting latency.

Design principles:

1) Determinism: the compiler must produce identical runtime blobs for identical inputs (rules + epoch metadata + nonces) so audit diffs are meaningful.
2) Compactness: runtime blobs should be optimized for fast evaluation (bitsets, compact role indexes), with separate human-readable manifests for debugging.
3) Signed evidence: every compiled output produces a signed audit bundle containing payload metadata, change set, and a verification signature (KMS-backed).
4) Backwards compatibility: SIEM export contract should be versioned. Old collectors can continue to parse v1 while new collectors accept v2.
5) Observability-first: include provenance fields (source ref, author, ticket) so policy decisions can be traced to changesets.

High-level architecture:

- Authoring surface: team members author RBAC rules in the policy DSL (design doc: policy-dsl.md). Changes are tracked via Git (policy-repo) and associated with a ticket (Jira).
- Compiler service: runs in CI and as a runtime service for ad-hoc compiles. Produces two outputs per compile: runtime_blob.tar (binary, indexed) and audit_bundle.json (signed).
- Runtime evaluators: small libraries in services that interpret runtime_blob (fast path) and emit compact decision events (allow/deny + rule_id + evaluation_latency_ns).
- Evidence exporter: collects audit_bundle and runtime decision events, enriches with request context, and ships to SIEM via standardized export contract.

Policy compiler contract (inputs):

- policy_set_id: string (e.g., policy-2025-01-12-23af)
- epoch: integer (monotonic compile counter)
- rules: list of rule objects (DSL source text as string; flattened list of rule_ids)
- role_map: mapping role -> set of rule_ids (compiler stores as index)
- metadata: author, git_ref, jira_ticket, change_reason
- compile_nonce: base64 (random)

Compiler outputs (artifact set):

1) runtime_blob.bin (binary) - opaque to SIEM but shipped to runtime. Includes:
   - header: policy_set_id, epoch, version, checksum
   - role index: role_id -> rule index range
   - rule table: compact encodings of predicates (resource id patterns, action enums, temporal bounds)
   - signature: signed over header+payload

2) audit_bundle.json - exported to evidence pipeline. Fields (all strings or arrays):
   - policy_set_id
   - epoch
   - compiled_at (ISO timestamp)
   - compiled_by (owner email/name)
   - git_ref
   - jira_ticket
   - change_summary (short)
   - rule_ids (list)
   - rule_hashes (list of sha256 strings, parallel to rule_ids)
   - role_map_snapshot (list of "role:role_id -> [rule_id,...]" strings)
   - deterministic_signature (base64)
   - compiler_version
   - export_version (e.g., siem-contract-v2)
   - required_parsers (list of parser ids)
   - provenance_refs (list of confluence/jira links)

Note: audit_bundle.json intentionally uses flat strings and lists so downstream loggers/Parsers can easily map to event fields.

SIEM export contract (for ingestion):

We will support two export modalities: bulk publish (daily/after-epoch) and streaming (on each compile for high-priority changes). The SIEM expects each audit bundle to map to a stable schema:
- event.type = "policy.compile"
- event.policy_set_id = string
- event.epoch = int
- event.signature = string
- event.rule_count = int
- event.rule_hash_list = string (comma-separated SHA256s)
- event.role_count = int
- event.author = string
- event.git_ref = string
- event.jira = string
- event.change_summary = string
- event.provenance_refs = string (semicolon-separated)

Contract versioning: export_version must be included; we recommend siem-contract-v2 which adds:
- event.delta_summary: string (list of added/removed roles/rules)
- event.epoch_parent: string (previous policy_set_id)

Runtime decision event enrichment (what evaluators emit):

- timestamp
- request_id
- actor_id (user/service)
- resource
- action
- decision: allow|deny|defer
- rule_id (string) — the rule that matched
- policy_set_id + epoch
- eval_latency_ns (int)
- rationale_tags (list of strings, optional: e.g., "prefix-cache-hit")

A decision event may be sampled in full for SIEM (all fields) or exported as an aggregated counter (per rule_id) to reduce ingestion costs. Sampling policy should be configurable per-tenant.

Signature and verifiability:

- Compiler signs audit_bundle and runtime_blob header using a KMS key (keys per-environment). Signature algorithm: RSA-PSS-SHA256 or ECDSA-P256 depending on environment.
- SIEM and forensics tooling should be able to call a verification service (public key endpoint) to validate a bundle signature.
- For cross-tenant evidence (Dedicated/Private), the exporter includes an evidence_proof envelope that contains the key_id and a trust chain reference.

Migration and rollout plan (high level):

Phase 0 — Engineering pilot (2–4 weeks)
- Implement compiler PoC and runtime evaluator library in a sandbox service.
- Generate audit_bundle examples and wire to a dev SIEM ingest endpoint.
- Validate signature verification tooling.

Phase 1 — Internal opt-in (4–8 weeks)
- Enable compiler for selected low-risk namespaces (internal tooling, feature flags).
- Add runtime evaluator to Canary route in serving-runtime.
- Begin streaming audit_bundle -> dev SIEM (siem-contract-v1).
- Run reconciliation: compare policy DSL vs runtime_blob hashes nightly; log mismatches to SEC-TRACK queue.

Phase 2 — Beta (8–12 weeks)
- Expand to more teams. Add role-based sampling and counterfactual logging (evaluate new policy but do not enforce) for a subset of traffic.
- Activate export_version siem-contract-v2 in parallel and update SIEM parsers to accept both v1 and v2.
- Implement automated drift alerts: if runtime decisions deviate from expected > X% for top N rules, trigger audit.

Phase 3 — Enforced rollout (3 months+)
- Require all new RBAC changes to go through the compiler CI gate.
- Migrate existing services by deploying runtime_blob evaluator libs and switching enforcement toggle.
- Retire legacy ad-hoc enforcement paths after a stabilization period and reconciliation verification.

Operational checklist for rollout:

- CI gating: compiler must run as a required check for policy-repo merges.
- Key management: testing KMS key rotation and signature verification prior to prod rollout.
- SIEM parser updates: ensure support for both contract versions and have fallback ingest logic.
- Sample budgets: configure per-tenant limits for decision event sampling; default conservative settings to avoid alert fatigue.
- Reconciliation job: nightly job that computes policy_set_id/epoch diff and produces a QA report (linked to Jira epic SEC-RBAC-MIGRATE).

Backout and safety measures:

- Canary traffic: start with 0.1% production traffic for 48–72 hours, watch decision latency and false-deny rate.
- Auto-fallback: evaluators must support runtime_blob fallback to previous epoch when signature verification fails or evaluation latency exceeds threshold.
- Emergency bypass: a signed short-lived policy (emergency_policy) that can be injected by SecOps to unblock critical flows; fully audited.

Monitoring and success criteria:

- Latency:Evaluator median decision latency < 0.8ms, p99 < 5ms (service-dependent).
- Drift: nightly drift rate < 0.1% for top 200 rules.
- Audit coverage: 100% of compiles produce audit_bundle; SIEM ingestion success > 99.9% within 24 hours.
- Forensics readiness: ability to reconstruct "policy state at time T" from audit bundles and runtime events.

Open questions and risks:

- How to encode very complex predicates (ML-based signals, cross-tenant references) in compact rule encodings? We may need to embed rule pointers to microservices instead of full predicate expansion.
- Cost of high-volume decision event streaming to SIEMs — need to model sample rates vs forensic utility.
- Private deployments with air-gapped environments require offline signature verification tooling and a lightweight exporter that can be pulled periodically.

Next steps (action items):

- [ ] Finalize compiler output formats (runtime_blob schema v1) — assigned: Devon Morales — due 2025-01-24
- [ ] Prototype signature envelope and verification service — assigned: Priya Nair — due 2025-02-07
- [ ] Create SIEM parser PR (splunk/syslog/elastic templates) — assigned: Owen Gallagher — due 2025-02-14
- [ ] Add nightly reconciliation job blueprint to automation repo — assigned: Marta Sokol — due 2025-02-10

Appendix A — Example audit_bundle.json (flattened):

policy_set_id: policy-2025-01-12-23af
epoch: 12
compiled_at: 2025-01-12T17:34:02Z
compiled_by: lena.zhang@redwood.ai
git_ref: refs/heads/rbac-v2-epoch12
jira_ticket: SEC-4321
change_summary: "remove dev-internal write on model:weights; add temporal window for support-bot role"
rule_ids: [R-001,R-128,R-140,...]
rule_hashes: [sha256-...,sha256-...,sha256-...]
role_map_snapshot: ["support-bot:[R-001,R-140]","dev-internal:[R-001]", ...]
deterministic_signature: BASE64_SIG
compiler_version: policy-compiler/0.9.3
export_version: siem-contract-v2
provenance_refs: [https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/sec/PR-56;https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/SEC-4321]

Appendix B — Parsing tips for SIEM teams:

- Treat rule_hashes as authoritative for content-level diffs; do not attempt to reconstruct rule bodies from hashes. Use git_ref + rule_id mapping to fetch human-readable source if available.
- For performance, ingest event.rule_hash_list as a single string and parse into array only for alerting queries.
- Use event.epoch to correlate runtime decision events to a specific compile snapshot.

Notes:

This draft aims to align enforcement, auditability, and SIEM expectations while minimizing runtime cost. Feedback requested on: semantics for emergency_policy, compact encoding proposals for ML predicates, and recommended sampling defaults for decision events.

-- Lena
